en: The Praise of One Hundred and Eight Names of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin, spoken by all the Tathāgatas;
translated by the Tripiṭaka Master of the Western Heaven, Chao San Dafu, Acting Minister of the Court of State Ceremonial.
Translated by the Dharma-transmitting Master, the Subject Shi Hu, by Imperial Decree.
At that time, all the Tathāgatas proclaimed the one hundred and eight names of the Universal Monarch, the Lord of Great Radiant Mantras of Immeasurable Merit.
Then he spoke this hymn of praise:
I take refuge in the Supreme Teacher, Lord of all the worlds,
who ever cherishes great compassion, And proclaims his great renown.
The Great Man endowed with the ten powers, Whose merit transcends the three realms and who is complete in all marks, Constantly revered by devas and humans,
he gathers in all sentient beings And acts as a great mass of merit for them.
He is also named Maheśvara, the Sovereign of All Buddha-Uṣṇīṣas who turns the wheel of all mantras;
he has perfectly realized the noble wisdom of the phrases of the True Dharma and is completely liberated in all things.
Ever the great sovereign, transcending all heavens,
he is the embodiment of great meditative concentration; viewing all sentient beings with equanimity,
he is endowed with boundless wisdom— neither real nor unreal.
Neither one nor two, he is called the Great Sage,
rare indeed in this world of gods and men; his nature is primordially quiescent,
pure and stainless, having skillfully entered the inexhaustible essence.
Vast and open, free from fear; neither interrupted nor destroyed, neither non-conceptual nor empty.
Able to relinquish all phenomena while remaining unattached like space—wondrous form is itself the form of emptiness.
Auspicious signs are auspicious omens; In tranquility, the constant and resolute mind gives rise to the wondrous Brahma-sound.
For those in that celestial realm, he is the sovereign image, vast and boundless; His merit is immeasurable.
Inconceivable by mind or speech, peerless and equal to the unequaled,
his true form is vast and boundless; ultimately invincible throughout infinite worlds, all pay him reverence.
Lord of all mantra-forms, this image is unprecedented;
it is a sublime image, a rare image. It is the divine eye and the third eye, the three true liberations, the word of truth, and true tranquility.
The real dharma abides in the limit of reality;
contemplating the wondrous Dharma-body, it is serene, eternal, firm, and enduring.
Its stainless nature is definitive, like the wind-god, the moon-god, the sun’s radiance, and the one of wondrous mind.
The three and six syllables of the text: one mantra, one syllable, one king, one wisdom, all-encompassing wisdom.
Sovereign, Great Sovereign, Brahmā, and Nārāyaṇa—these are the single Buddha and the single Dharma-characteristic.
Dwelling for a day among a multitude, in a single session and with a single correspondence,
throughout all worlds, he eloquently discourses on the various wondrous Dharmas;
by means of this light of supernormal power, he transforms light everywhere.
With the power of great light and majestic virtue,
he is the Lord of all celestial rulers and the Lord of all Buddha-dharmas;
he is the Lord of the wisdom of all dharmas and a mass of inexhaustible merit— this is called the One Hundred and Eight [Names].
The Praise of the One Hundred and Eight Names of the Buddha-Uṣṇīṣa-Cakravartin Spoken by All Tathāgatas.
